# Coherent Replay Hamiltonian Learning

This repository develops local full-waveform Hamiltonian learning with inverse-precision unknown-evolution cost under coherent prefix replay and charged known inverse controls. The science is organized by topic, and each claim has one authoritative proof location.

## Scientific reading routes

- Start with README.md for the question, resource summary and direct routes.
- Read science/model.md for the exact Pauli-pattern, geometry, polynomial, uniform-error and operational-access assumptions. Physical time is normalized here.
- Read science/local_response.md for the right-echo identity, quasi-local shell interaction moments, exact local second-order remainder and signed product-process estimator.
- Read science/reconstruction.md for temporal conditioning, one-sided endpoint stencils, degree-zero handling, interpolation, rounding, guarded controllers and adaptive confidence.
- Read science/resources.md for the paid initializer, degree and precision cost, inverse compilation, workspace, output bits, timing and noise budgets, and lower bound.
- Read science/interpretation.md for the exact endpoint-indistinguishable noncommuting example, finite-shot findings, physical use and implementation comparison.
- Read references/RELATED_WORK.md and references/references.bib for attributed mechanisms, primary-source versions and task/access distinctions.
- Read verification/README.md before running verification/verify_protocol.py; compare with verification/expected/protocol.json.

## Study route

The single educational anchor is Nielsen and Chuang, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information, 10th Anniversary Edition (2010).

- Read learning/README.md for the source identity and available routes.
- Read learning/BRIDGE.md for the relevant anchor sections, notation, a complete commuting one-qubit example and the steps needed for local noncommuting waveform learning.
- Follow learning/MILESTONES.md for M01–M30: 11 background/preliminaries targets and 19 narrative/innovation targets. Its dependencies and source pointers define a common conceptual map of the project.
- Use the canonical science pages for exact statements and proofs. The anchor supplies foundations; specialized primary papers supply the attributed research ingredients.

## Retrieval distinctions to preserve

The output error is the maximum uniform coefficient-function error, not global process distance and not monomial-coordinate error. The pulse horizon, local strength, degree and geometry must be carried with asymptotic claims. Constants can grow with the horizon.

The known inverse acts before each unknown forward prefix. The schedule clock restarts while the quantum register stays coherent. Product preparation occurs only at the start of the whole shot; intermediate input states may be entangled. The trusted controller's gates, ancillary workspace, numerical precision and classical data are charged.

The logarithmic n dependence is the number of parallel experimental shots. The output, preparation, measurement, control gates and classical data have their extensive costs. A fixed grid does not mean fixed timing accuracy.

The initialization theorem is an imported, paid ingredient. Its actual fixed-size probe regions differ from its growing analytic approximation region. Do not replace the former by uncharged dense tomography of the latter.

The precision exponent is optimal under coherent access. Independent-prefix waveform learning has weaker access and a weak-dephasing extension not provided by the present theorem. Coherent replay and learned-inverse amplification are established mechanisms. No first-in-field or universal classical-speedup claim is made.

The finite-shot experiment uses an illustrative supplied initial model and instance-specific tuning. It does not execute the conservative universal constants or the paid initializer. Its multinomial aggregation represents all reported physical shots. Twelve observed successful seeds are not a rigorous confidence certificate, and the large sample cost is not a practical crossover.

Fixed per-pair control or replay noise eventually violates the shrinking error budget. The coherent theorem does not establish noisy open-system waveform learning or a device's actual calibration quality.
